items.title: Decoding the loopy physics of hula hooping with high-tech earthquake sensors
items.abstract: Hula hooping may be literal child's play, but as it turns out, the physics behind the gym-class staple is so complicated that scientists have spent decades trying to understand how the hula hoop defies gravity.

items.title: Identical vesicles, different behaviors: Model reveals how spontaneous asymmetry gives rise to lifelike behavior
items.abstract: In nonreciprocal active matter, agents act differently on each other, seemingly in violation of Newton's third law. This principle can result in various active matter traits, such as self-propulsion, molecular regulation and collective motion.
